To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coherent multiple partonic scatterings in lepton-nuclear and hadron-nuclear collisions lead to nuclear shadowing of structure functions and nuclear suppression of single hadron and dihadron production in high energy hadron-nuclear reactions.

(i) coherent multiple scattering in the nuclear target can be described in a unified framework in terms of the Glauber model and the dipole model; (ii) this framework can be used to calculate the nuclear shadowing in deep inelastic lepton-nuclei scattering and nuclear suppression in hadron-nuclei scattering at RHIC and the LHC; (iii) the nuclear suppression is a function of the transverse momentum of the hadrons and the nuclear size; (iv)

coherent multiple scattering in l+A and p+A reactions can be described in a unified way by using a simple model of the parton distributions in a nucleus, and that the nuclear attenuation effects are large enough to be observed in the RHIC data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the coherent multiple scattering with several nucleon targets, which is a key ingredient in the understanding of the physics of high-energy lepton-nuclei and hadron-nuclear collisions.

a systematic investigation of the effects of multiple scattering of quarks and gluons on the structure functions of nuclei and on single and double inclusive spectra of hadrons in high energy lepton and hadron collisions with nuclear targets.
the physics of coherent multiple parton (or hadron) scattering in high-energy nuclear collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coherent multiple scattering is an essential ingredient in understanding nuclear effects in high-energy reactions.
the nuclear effects on the single and dihadron production in p+A collisions can be described in terms of a coherent multiple parton model.
the nuclear attenuation in p+A and l+A collisions can be described within the coherent multiple scattering approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coherent multiple scattering in heavy ion collisions is an important effect which can be used to study the structure of nuclear matter.
coherent multiple scattering in the initial state is a crucial effect in the description of the hadronic final state at RHIC and LHC.
the multiple scattering with several nucleon is an important dynamical mechanism which can be studied at RHIC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear effects in p+A reactions are qualitatively similar to those in l+A reactions, but quantitatively different.
nuclear effects are not only a source of systematic uncertainties, but also a tool to probe the QCD dynamics in a new kinematic regime.
the coherent multiple partonic scattering is the dominant effect in nuclear attenuation at RHIC and the LHC energies.
